newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BUBKA PRODUCES HIS BEST UNDER PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BUBKA PRODUCES HIS BEST UNDER PRESSURE.

text.p: Sergei Bubka produced his best performance under the greatest pressure on Sunday when he defied age and injury to win the world pole vault title for a sixth successive time.

"I am the only person to have won all six world championships," said the 33-year-old Ukrainian. "This is perhaps not my best title but it was the most difficult. It was not easy but I'm really happy."
Bubka did not start last year's Atlanta Olympic competition after sustaining an Achilles tendon injury and the injury has disrupted his training this year.
He started on Sunday by clearing 5.70 metres with his second attempt, managed 5.91, again with his second try then watched while Russian Maksim Tarasov, the 1992 Olympic champion, vaulted 5.96.
Bubka passed at 5.96, going straight for 6.01.
As the capacity crowd of 60,000 roared their appreciation, Bubka soared over the bar with his first effort to clinch the gold medal.
"That 6.01 was one of his best jumps that I have ever seen," said Tarasov. "It's amazing to see him win six titles at world championships."

The man who has set 17 outdoor world records thought an 18th would provide a suitable conclusion to a memorable performance and tried 6.15 metres, one centimetre above his three-year-old mark mark of 6.14
He started to run but stopped on the runway as spectators whistled in frustration.
"I was not disappointed by the reaction of the public," he said. "They wanted to see a world record. But they must understand that I was just coming back from injury."
Bubka was greeted with loud applause when he entered the post-event news conference.
He explained that he had been forced to take anti-inflammatory medicine after training and again after the qualifying round here.

"At every training session, I was always thinking about the tendon," he said. "Coming here was a big risk after the injury. It was a difficult decision but once I decided to come, I focused on the gold medal.
"My main secret is that I love sport. I was born for sport and I always want to be the best."
